messages.content:
Diagnosis:

The test `testGetLineNumberWithCR` creates a CSVParser with input containing carriage returns "\r" as line separators, and sets the format with `.withLineSeparator("\r")`.

The CSVParser.getLineNumber() delegates the call to lexer.getLineNumber(), which further calls in.getLineNumber(), where in is an instance of ExtendedBufferedReader.

The ExtendedBufferedReader maintains a lineCounter incremented in its read() and readLine() methods.

Inspecting ExtendedBufferedReader.read(), we see it only increments lineCounter when encountering a newline character '\n' (LF). It does not increment for a sole carriage return '\r', which is the line separator used in the test.

The readLine() method calls the superclass BufferedReader.readLine(), which treats '\r', '\n', and '\r\n' as line terminators and strips them. After reading a line, the ExtendedBufferedReader increments lineCounter unconditionally for every read line; this works because BufferedReader.readLine() processes all kinds of terminators.

However, if the code uses the read() method instead of readLine(), line counting will only increment on '\n'. The test likely relies on reading lines based on read() or the incremental line counting in general. Since the input uses carriage returns ('\r') alone as line separators, the line counting fails to increment for those, showing an incorrect line number.

The current bug report states this inconsistency: ExtendedBufferedReader increments line count only on '\n' in read(), but readLine() increments line count assuming BufferedReader reads all line break types. To fix, ExtendedBufferedReader should also count carriage returns '\r' as line terminators in read().

Hence, the bug is the inconsistent handling of EOL characters in ExtendedBufferedReader.read(), where '\r' is not considered a line break, causing CSVParser.getLineNumber() to report incorrect line numbers on inputs with carriage-return line separators.

Recent bug reports do not provide further relevant info and can be ignored for this fault localization.

This explains the failure of the test when using line separators "\r". The line counting logic in ExtendedBufferedReader.read() is incomplete and needs to be adjusted to handle both '\n' and '\r' as line separators.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
